name: Wood engraving
summary: A relief print from the end grain of a hard wood, cut with a burin. The fine white lines make the tone.
how: Cut the end grain of boxwood with a burin; the line can be as fine as 0.1 mm.
Cut white lines for the light, so that the printed black stays solid between them.
Make tone with the width and spacing of the white lines, not with a screen.
Print with a letterpress, in one black ink, on smooth paper.

origin.note: Thomas Bewick developed the technique at the end of the 18th century.

adoptions.via: Thomas Bewick publishes the first volume of A History of British Birds, with wood engravings in the text.
The Dalziel Brothers start a London firm that cuts blocks for the illustrated press.
